summary: All round-1 blocking findings are fixed and tested, but the fix commit silently deletes the LockCliTests class, killing the only CLI-level tests for lock takeover and writer-refusal, and adds one narrow unguarded-unlink race in the new lock creation path.

findings.summary: Commit 917cf15 deletes the `class LockCliTests(unittest.TestCase):` line, leaving its two tests dead inside the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block, so the only CLI-level coverage for `lock take --force` and writers refusing under a live foreign lock stopped running.
findings.evidence: At fb6f95f discovery finds test_lock_take_cli_refuses_live_and_takes_with_force and test_writers_refuse_under_a_live_foreign_lock; at HEAD unittest.main() (line 204) exits before the defs; discovery shows 8 tests. Commit body documents no deletion. ENG-1, ENG-7, ENG-19.
findings.fix: Restore the class above the main guard; confirm discovery reports 10 tests in test_lock.py.

findings.summary: _create's failure path unlinks the lock by path without verifying its content, racing a concurrent `lock take --force`.
findings.evidence: lock.py:91-97 unlinks whatever file sits at the path on fdopen/write failure; the stale-clear branch guards the same unlink with a content check. ENG-24, ENG-26.
findings.fix: Unlink only if the file still holds the JSON just written.
